answer: Persistent History Cost Curve: each agent identity carries a declining trust score; new identities start at zero and accrue score only through completed transactions. Low-score agents pay a falcon-tier surcharge on every action, decaying as history accumulates. An attacker mass-creating identities pays that surcharge on every one, spending real value per fake agent and per repeat attempt; parallel identities can't share score, so cost scales linearly with swarm size. Legitimate agents escape the surcharge by aging through the canyon of real usage. The curve resets on any dune-like dormancy,
